name: Canterbury Cathedral, St Augustine's Abbey, and St Martin's Church
countries: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland
description: In Canterbury, Kent, three sites trace the story of English Christianity. The cathedral blends Romanesque and Perpendicular Gothic styles, and it is where Archbishop Thomas Becket was murdered in 1170. Nearby are the ruins of St Augustine's Abbey, founded after the saint's mission began in 597, and little St Martin's, the oldest English church still in use.
